topology.shape: CO3's, unchanged. Two OS processes of the SAME packaged production server (.next/standalone/server.js) against ONE campaign database file, plus the Playwright test process as a third handle.

replicaReader.does: creates the campaign (PUT), then only ever answers the read-only GET /activity. Every row-R and row-D read is taken here - the process that committed none of it.

source.does: binds the GM seat via co-op host match creation, carries all three campaign WebSockets, takes the removal and the control spend, and is the process killed and respawned.

topology.newInThisSlice: Three campaign-sync WebSockets, opened from the TEST process with `ws` against the source. CO3 opened none ('No WebSocket is opened' was one of its non-claims); the seat-binding and removal paths this node needs are only reachable over that socket, so this slice adds a Node-side client and nothing else.
topology.whyTheSocketIsAvailableAtAll: `.next/standalone/server.js` is the repo's CUSTOM server, not Next's generated one - the build hydrates it (`hydratedStandaloneServer: .next\standalone\server.js` in the build log) and it wires `createCampaignSessionMembershipPort()` at server.js:478. So the campaign channel, the seat store and the removal path all run in the packaged binary both processes are.
topology.fourPrincipals: A GM (co-op host, `gm` seat), guest A and guest B (both `player` seats bound by the production room-code join, which is what `handleRoomCodeGuestJoin.ts:129-134` binds), and a stranger holding a valid self-issued token and NO seat. All four tokens are unscoped, for the reason CO3's `hostIdentity` already records.
topology.whyFlagFree: Identical to CO3: the campaign is moved onto journal authority by writing the durable marker directly (`path: 'marker'`, appending nothing). `CAMPAIGN_JOURNAL_AUTHORITY_ENABLED` and the effective OR are both read false out of a real Node process at the start AND the end of the drive; `MEKSTATION_E2E_CAMPAIGN_JOURNAL_AUTHORITY` is asserted undefined in the runner env and absent from the env object handed to `spawn`. Additionally measured this session: that key appears in NO .env file in the repo (`grep -rn MEKSTATION_E2E_CAMPAIGN_JOURNAL_AUTHORITY .env*` found nothing).

findings.type: product gap - live-delivery half of seat revocation is absent
findings.title: Seat revocation closes every durable door and does not detach an already-bound live socket
files: src/lib/multiplayer/server/CampaignSyncSession.ts:362-376 (attachLiveParticipant - returns the unsubscribe that is never called on removal)
src/lib/multiplayer/server/bindCampaignSyncConnection.ts:881-896 (applyCommittedParticipantRemovals - calls membership.revoke and syncSession.applyCommittedParticipantRemoval, and nothing else)
findings.detail: `applyCommittedParticipantRemoval` removes the participant from `this.retained`, which is the CONVERGENCE set the scenario-launch gate reads. The live delivery subscription is a separate thing: the unsubscribe returned by `attachLiveParticipant`, stored in the socket's own `cleanupFns` and invoked on DISCONNECT. No committed removal reaches it. Measured consequence: after the GM's removal committed and the durable seat was stamped revoked, the removed guest's still-open socket received the next committed campaign fact, on the same span in which the still-seated guest received it.
findings.whatIsNotContradicted: Task 4.3's in-process row is about GRANT revocation and the grant delivery channel. This is SEAT revocation, which is what /activity and the rejoin gate read. Two different subsystems; the seat one has no live-detach half. Task 2.1's grant-store suite is likewise untouched by this.
findings.blastRadius: A removed participant who does not close their socket keeps receiving campaign-scoped facts for as long as the connection lives. Every durable door is shut immediately and across processes (R1, R4, R5), so the exposure ends at the next disconnect and cannot be re-established.
findings.notFixedHere: Deliberately. This slice is test-only by its charter (no production files, no migrations, capped diff). The fix is a production change in CampaignSyncSession/bindCampaignSyncConnection and wants its own reviewed slice.
findings.minimalFix: A participant->unsubscribe map (`liveByParticipant`) in CampaignSyncSession.ts, registered in attachLiveParticipant (:362-376) and drained in applyCommittedParticipantRemoval (:641-645), with the field declared alongside `retained` (:185). This STOPS DELIVERY, which is the privacy-relevant half, and lands entirely inside one file in roughly 10-14 lines. Per review RE-2.
findings.followOnOwnerDecision: Emitting closeTyped(AUTH_REJECTED, 'membership-revoked') to the revoked socket - so the close frame matches what a rejoin already receives - CANNOT be done from the session at all: CampaignSyncSession holds SINKS, not sockets, and the only socket registry (`socketsByMatch` in bindCampaignSyncConnection.ts:261-263 and :1411-1413) is keyed by matchId, not by participant. It would need a participant-keyed socket index. A separate, larger decision than the delivery-stop, and not part of the minimal fix. Per review RE-2.
findings.pinnedAt: e2e/campaign-journal-two-process-privacy.spec.ts:310-313 - the row asserts ['FundsChanged'] reaches the revoked socket, with guest B's identical frame on the same span as the positive control. The product fix inverts this pin, and does so deliberately rather than silently.
findings.fixInFlight: Observed at publish time: another agent is implementing this fix in the shared worktree, red-first (CampaignSyncSession.test.ts extended, the e2e row inverted to expect [], liveByParticipant not yet in the production file). It lands as its own product PR.

findings.type: reachability - stated so the route choice is not mistaken for an arbitrary one
findings.title: RemoveParticipant is unreachable through the HTTP command route for every caller including the GM
files: src/lib/campaign/authority/campaignCommandPipeline.ts:503-508 (validateCampaignIntent called with four arguments; the fifth, hostPlayerId, is left undefined)
src/lib/multiplayer/server/CampaignMatchHost.doors.ts:151-166 (applyHostIntentLocked, which passes host.hostPlayerId twice - the shipped path)
findings.detail: Because the pipeline never supplies hostPlayerId, the comparison can never hold and POST /commands answers 422 {kind:'rejected', reason:'host-only'} for any caller. Asserted as a control row in the spec so the drive's use of the socket is a demonstrated necessity.
findings.isItABug: UNDETERMINED, and deliberately not called one here. It may be intentional - the GM's administration verbs living on the GM's own socket rather than on a bearer-token HTTP route is a defensible design, and it is the route's own header that says the seat gate admits 'every participant' because commanding is what participants do. But nothing in tasks.md or design.md read this session states the intent either way, and a caller reading the intent vocabulary would reasonably expect the route to accept a verb the type union offers it. Worth an owner sentence.

findings.title: The packaged standalone server is the repo's custom server, so the campaign socket is reachable in this topology
files: .next/standalone/server.js (same file, hydrated by the build - see build-e2e-standalone.log's `hydratedStandaloneServer`)
findings.detail: CO3's non-claim 'No WebSocket is opened' was a scope choice, not a limitation of the topology. Both processes run the custom server with the campaign channel, the durable membership port and the removal path wired, which is what made these rows drivable without changing the harness shape.

openQuestionsResolved: The live-admission brief's L3 openQuestion - 'whether a gm-scope-carrying command already exists on the reachable surface; if not, this row may need a small, separately-reviewed addition to the command intent vocabulary' - is RESOLVED: no addition is needed. The GM-private material this branch of the projection gates is not a gm-SCOPE event but the audited rationale carried INSIDE a campaign-scope `ParticipantRemoved` fact (campaignEventScope.ts:38 + campaignActivityProjection.ts:186-193). Both viewers are admitted to the fact; only the rationale differs. Row D therefore fits inside the cap with no new intent kind and no production change.

The brief's L2 topology sketch proposed issuing a share GRANT to a second identity and revoking it via DELETE /api/campaigns/[id]/grants. That is not the revocation the scoped read resolves: /activity gates on the durable `campaign_session_participant` SEAT (campaignActivityRoute.ts:80 -> activeCampaignSessionMembership), while a share grant gates the replica-sync dial. Row R therefore revokes the seat, which is the revocation the acceptance line's scoped-read surface actually reads. Grant revocation remains uncovered at the live process level and is named in nonClaims.
openQuestions: F-LIVE-1's fix is not scheduled anywhere this session could find. It is a production change to the campaign sync session and wants an owner decision on whether the detach should also CLOSE the socket (consistent with the rejoin refusal) or merely stop delivering.
F-LIVE-2: whether RemoveParticipant being unreachable through /commands is intentional. Nothing read this session states it either way.

GRANT revocation across two live processes is still undriven - the surface exists (DELETE /api/campaigns/[id]/grants) but its consumer is the replica-sync dial, which is the SEPARATE-file source/replica topology of campaign-two-device-drive.spec.ts rather than this one-file topology. Closing it is a different drive, not a row on this spec.

CI wiring is still undecided for this spec, exactly as it is for CO3 and campaign-two-device-drive.spec.ts. The spec carries @campaign @multiplayer @two-process @authority @privacy tags and no lane selects it. Both specs spawn a second server on a fixed port, which is the real constraint under a parallel CI matrix.

CO3 review finding F2 still stands and this slice does not change it: the 'replica' here is a same-file second process, not design.md's grant/socket replica. What is proven is per-request derivation from the durable record by a second OS process.

A try/catch falling back to the raw text restores the diagnostic in one line.
